author: philly leader
title: Eagles prepare for key Black Friday matchup against division-leading Bears
text:
Friday’s game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Chicago Bears will be held at 3 p.m. on Black Friday, featuring a “Back in Black” theme that encourages fans to wear black. Both teams enter the matchup with an 8-3 record, making it a significant contest with playoff implications.
The Bears have improved their performance this season after hiring Ben Johnson as head coach and focusing on rebuilding through the NFL Draft. Quarterback Caleb Williams has shown progress, supported by upgrades to the offensive line.
Eagles Offensive Coordinator Kevin Patullo addressed recent struggles: “That’s disappointing and that’s frustrating, but it’s going to give us an opportunity on a short week to get out there and get after the Bears,” Patullo said. “So, there’s a lot to be encouraged by. But at the same time, when those things happen, when you go into the locker room after the game, the frustration levels are high, right? We know how close we were and if those things don’t go the way they go, it’s a whole other outcome.”
The Eagles’ running game has not gained momentum this season. The team continues efforts to involve Saquon Barkley more effectively against what is expected to be a strong Bears defense.
Chicago leads the NFL with 24 takeaways this season despite some injuries at linebacker. Their aggressive defense puts pressure on opponents’ offenses and features an improved secondary led by safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson. Under head coach Nick Sirianni, Philadelphia is 40-2 when winning the turnover battle.
Defensively for Philadelphia, coordinator Vic Fangio prepares his unit for Chicago’s big-play offense that includes wide receivers D.J. Moore, Rome Odunze, rookie Luther Burden III; tight ends Cole Kmet and Colston Loveland; and running backs D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai. Safety Sydney Brown noted: “They do a great job at play-action, they throw the ball well and have talent, and the scheme is really tough.” Reed Blankenship added: “They also try to fool you with a lot of eye candy (pre-snap motion, etc.) so you have to trust your eyes and have great communication.”
Penalties remain an issue for both teams; Philadelphia averages 7.6 penalties per game while Chicago averages 7.9.
Caleb Williams has led five comeback wins for Chicago this season in games where they trailed late in regulation.
Chicago ranks second in rushing yards per game (142) with 48 runs of ten or more yards this year. The Eagles aim to avoid negative plays as too many three-and-outs have hampered their offense recently.
Philadelphia leads the league in red zone touchdown efficiency on offense while ranking third-best defensively in that area; Chicago ranks mid-pack offensively (16th) but lower defensively (26th).
Weather could play a role as wind gusts up to 30 mph are forecasted for Lincoln Financial Field—potentially affecting special teams play and passing effectiveness.
